title: ആകാശഗംഗയും ചാണകവണ്ടും തമ്മിലെന്ത്? Dung Beetles Navigate by the Milky Way #malayalam #facts #insect
description:
Dung Beetles Navigate by the Milky Way
Nocturnal dung beetles (specifically Scarabaeus satyrus) are the first known insects to use the Milky Way for orientation, using the bright band of stars as a celestial compass to navigate in a straight line while rolling their dung balls. 
Milky Way as a Compass:
Researchers discovered that these beetles use the Milky Way, not individual stars, as a reference point to maintain a straight path when rolling their dung balls. 
Orientation in the Dark:
Studies in a planetarium showed that beetles could navigate effectively under a simulated Milky Way, even when other celestial cues were absent, like the moon. 
First Insect to Use the Milky Way:
This finding is significant because it's the first documented use of the Milky Way for orientation in the animal kingdom, and specifically the first time it's been proven for an insect.
